units.rhetorical_move: names the missing term and the reason it must be added
units.function: opens by saying what the usual analysis leaves out

original_instantiations: Services belong inside the appraisal so the real worth of a scheme is not missed.
The omitted term is put back so the judgement covers the whole of the scheme.

units.source_excerpt: Ecosystem services should be included in the cost benefit analysis of land use development projects in order to assess true values of them comprehensively.
units.reusable_pattern: State the missing term, then the purpose the inclusion serves.
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the phrase true values of them comprehensively

units.rhetorical_move: splits the work into two time horizons
units.function: announces the two models before either is described

original_instantiations: One model covers the near period and the other the far period, and both feed the same appraisal.
The two horizons are built separately and then joined to the same comparison.

units.source_excerpt: We establish a short run model and a long run model of ecosystem service evaluation respectively, and incorporate the environmental cost into the cost benefit analysis.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the two horizons first, then say what both of them enter.
reusable_elements: a shared verb for both models
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the two horizons as interchangeable

units.rhetorical_move: widens the meaning of the cost across three concerns
units.function: says the far-horizon cost is not the same quantity as the near one

original_instantiations: The far-horizon cost grows from a money figure into three separate concerns.
What counts as cost in the far period is wider than what counts in the near period.

units.source_excerpt: we develop the meaning of the environmental cost from the economic value of short run replacement cost to the cost of three aspects
units.reusable_pattern: Mark the widening with from and to, and list the new concerns.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the three concerns are measured in money

units.rhetorical_move: reports a verdict and reads it as confirmation
units.function: lets the case outcome stand in for a test of the model

original_instantiations: The return still beats the cost after the adjustment, and that is taken to confirm the model.
A surviving verdict is offered as evidence that the model holds.

units.source_excerpt: the total benefit of the construction project of thermal power stations is still greater than the total cost even after the adjusting and optimizing the model, which indicates that the construction of Tennessee thermal power stations has large real value
units.reusable_pattern: Give the comparison, then a which-clause that reads it as support.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat one surviving verdict as a full validation

units.rhetorical_move: cites a warning and draws the consequence
units.function: turns a published claim into the reason for the work

original_instantiations: A cited paper warns that the services are being lost, so a model that can price the loss is needed.
The warning is quoted and the requirement follows from it.

units.source_excerpt: So an ecological services model that can evaluate environmental cost in different time scale and can be applied to assess the influence of a certain project is required.
units.reusable_pattern: End the background with the requirement the warning creates.
prohibited_generalizations: do not invent the content of the citation

units.rhetorical_move: restates the assigned task in two steps
units.function: separates building the model from using it

original_instantiations: First the cost is priced so the real cost can be measured, then the cost enters the appraisal.
The task is split into measuring and then judging.

units.source_excerpt: We are asked to build an ecological services model to evaluate the environmental cost so as to measure the true economic cost of land use development projects.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate the task with so as to linking the model to its purpose.
prohibited_generalizations: do not add tasks the problem did not set

units.rhetorical_move: lists the work as a sequence of bullets
units.function: lets the reader see the order of the paper at once

features.transition: in the short run ... in the long run
original_instantiations: The bullets run from assumptions to the near model, the far model, the two cases and the test.
Each bullet names one piece of work and nothing more.

units.source_excerpt: In order to solve the problem, we did the following work
units.reusable_pattern: Announce the list, then give one bullet per piece of work.
prohibited_generalizations: do not let a bullet carry more than one job

units.rhetorical_move: defines the two horizons by what each measures
units.function: stops the time split from being read as a calendar split

original_instantiations: The near model prices only the damage of the present period, while the far model also prices the damage that accumulates.
The horizon is fixed by the measurement, not by the length of the project.

units.source_excerpt: The short run model only measures the cost of environmental damage in the current period, while the long run model also considers the cost of damage to sustainable development and ecosystem after environmental degradation over time.
units.reusable_pattern: Define each horizon by the damage it counts, joined by while.
prohibited_generalizations: do not read the split as a fixed number of years

units.rhetorical_move: states what the builders ignore
units.function: fences the model by naming the motive it assumes

original_instantiations: The builders are taken to chase profit and to ignore any good the project does to the environment.
The assumption removes the positive side so only the cost remains.

units.source_excerpt: Project builders maximize profits, regardless of the positive environmental benefit brought by land use projects.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the motive, then exclude the rest with regardless of.
prohibited_generalizations: do not later count the benefit the assumption excludes

units.rhetorical_move: defers the numbers to a later place
units.function: tells the reader the table holds names, not values

original_instantiations: The symbols are named here and their values are promised for later.
The table is marked as a list of names rather than a list of results.

units.source_excerpt: Where we define the main parameters while specific value of those parameters will be given later.
units.reusable_pattern: Define the symbols and postpone the values in the same sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the table as a source of numbers

units.rhetorical_move: marks the model as provisional
units.function: warns that time is left out for now

original_instantiations: The basic model adds the environmental cost and leaves time out for the moment.
The reader is told the omission is temporary.

units.source_excerpt: In general, we establish the basic model by incorporating the environmental cost into cost benefit analysis, which does not involve the influence of time provisionally.
units.reusable_pattern: Build the model, then mark the omission as provisional.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the provisional model as the final one

units.rhetorical_move: names the method and the quantity it recovers
units.function: justifies the choice by what it makes measurable

original_instantiations: The method is chosen so the cost of restoring the system can be stated in money.
The purpose clause tells why this method and not another.

units.source_excerpt: we adopt replacement cost method to assess the ability of ecosystem services in order to measure the monetary value of the cost of making the ecosystem revert to original standard after being polluted
units.reusable_pattern: Name the method, then the quantity it is meant to recover.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the method prices every kind of damage

units.rhetorical_move: explains the multiplication
units.function: says the charge applies only past the carrying capacity

original_instantiations: The cost is the excess pollution times the treatment cost per unit.
Only the part beyond the carrying capacity is charged.

units.source_excerpt: The replacement cost is calculated by multiplying the amount of pollution discharged by the construction project beyond the environmental carrying capacity and the treatment cost per unit of pollution together.
units.reusable_pattern: State the product and name both factors.
prohibited_generalizations: do not charge the pollution that nature handles

units.rhetorical_move: splits the benefit and defines each part
units.function: keeps the social part in money

original_instantiations: One part is the value of the extra jobs and the other is the value of the better image.
Both parts are stated as money so they can be added.

units.source_excerpt: One is B21, the monetary value of the increase of employment rate because of the land use project. The other is B22, the monetary value of the improvement of city image resulted from the project.
units.reusable_pattern: Introduce the two parts with one is and the other is.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave either part unpriced

units.rhetorical_move: credits a theory and states the widening
units.function: says the old cost is only the narrow case

original_instantiations: Against the cited theory, the cost grows past the narrow money reading.
The old definition is kept as the special case of the new one.

units.source_excerpt: Based on the theory of the economic analysis of environmental pollution cost, considering the impact of environmental degradation in the long run, the concept of environmental pollution cost expands in three aspects compared with the original health-economic understanding of pollution cost.
units.reusable_pattern: Credit the source, then say how the concept widens.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the citation

units.rhetorical_move: explains why money is abandoned
units.function: justifies the change of method

original_instantiations: Because the far-horizon cost cannot be priced, another method has to be used.
The difficulty is the reason for the switch.

units.source_excerpt: As these environmental costs are difficult to be measured by money in long run, we have to use another method to evaluate these costs.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the difficulty, then the forced change of method.
prohibited_generalizations: do not pretend the new method still yields money

units.rhetorical_move: builds the matrix from a literature count
units.function: turns search results into relative importance

original_instantiations: The relative weight of each indicator is taken from how often the literature mentions it.
A keyword search supplies the ratios the matrix needs.

units.source_excerpt: After searching keywords on Google Scholar, we obtained the results. So we estimate the relative importance of each index in the matrix.
units.reusable_pattern: Report the search, then the estimate it supports.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat a hit count as a measured preference

units.rhetorical_move: states the consistency rule and the fallback
units.function: tells the reader when the matrix must be rebuilt

original_instantiations: Below the threshold the matrix stands, and above it the matrix is rebuilt.
The rule names both the passing case and the failing case.

units.source_excerpt: If CR< 0.1, it is considered that the degree of inconsistency is within the acceptable range, so it passes the consistency test. If it can't pass the test, we will modify J.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the passing condition and the repair in two if-sentences.
prohibited_generalizations: do not skip the repair step

units.rhetorical_move: sets the two costs equal by belief
units.function: makes the equality a judgement rather than a result

original_instantiations: Because the environmental cost is now counted, it is judged as important as the economic cost.
The equal weight is a belief, not a calculation.

units.source_excerpt: Since environmental cost is taken into account, we believe that environmental cost is as important as economic cost for the examiner.
units.reusable_pattern: State the belief and the equality it produces.
prohibited_generalizations: do not present the equality as data

units.rhetorical_move: converts the benefit onto the same scale
units.function: explains why the ranking is repeated

original_instantiations: The benefit is ranked the same way as the cost so the two can be compared.
The repeated ranking is what makes the comparison possible.

units.source_excerpt: we conducted the same ranking process towards the benefit as the economic cost's above to make cost and benefit comparable
units.reusable_pattern: Say the process is repeated and name the comparability it buys.
prohibited_generalizations: do not compare a money figure with a score

units.rhetorical_move: assigns one method to each project
units.function: matches the horizon to the size

original_instantiations: The near model goes to the small local project and the far model goes to the large national one.
Size and horizon are paired on purpose.

units.source_excerpt: one is a short run model application to a small community-based project, the other is a long run model application to a large national project
units.reusable_pattern: Pair each model with the project it is applied to.
prohibited_generalizations: do not apply both models to both projects

units.rhetorical_move: frames the case as a decision for an officer
units.function: gives the model a user inside the story

original_instantiations: An officer has to weigh the scheme and decide whether to grant it.
The case is told as a decision someone must make.

units.source_excerpt: Now the land planning bureau's officer should measure the cost and benefit of the project to decide whether the project should be granted.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the person who decides and the decision itself.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the case without a decision maker

units.rhetorical_move: flags a contrast with the standard practice
units.function: uses the contrast to justify the large number

original_instantiations: The standard mills use far less water, but the small mills use vastly more.
The contrast explains why the computed cost is so high.

units.source_excerpt: It should be pointed out that the advanced paper mills in developed countries only discharge about 10 cubic meters of water per ton of paper production. However, there are a large number of small nonstandard paper mills which need about 1 million cubic meters per ton of paper.
units.reusable_pattern: Point out the contrast and let however carry the exception.
prohibited_generalizations: do not smooth the contrast away

units.rhetorical_move: reads the comparison as a rejection
units.function: adds that the far horizon would only make it worse

original_instantiations: The cost already beats the benefit, and the far horizon is not even counted.
The rejection is stated and then strengthened.

units.source_excerpt: We can see that the cost of the private paper mill is far greater than its benefit when only the replacement cost of COD is taken into account. The addition of short run environmental cost has made us reject construction project, not to mention the long run environmental cost.
units.reusable_pattern: State the comparison, the decision, then the further reason.
prohibited_generalizations: do not soften the rejection

units.rhetorical_move: delivers the verdict in the officer's voice
units.function: closes the case with the decision

original_instantiations: The officer has to refuse the request.
The verdict is given as an obligation.

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, our officer in land planning bureau must reject the private entrepreneur's request.
units.reusable_pattern: Close the case with therefore and a modal of obligation.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the verdict implied

units.rhetorical_move: justifies the chosen project with a list of reasons
units.function: makes the selection look deliberate

original_instantiations: The project is chosen for its scale, its long dominance, its estimable return and its environmental impact.
Each reason is a separate bullet.

units.source_excerpt: we select to analyze construction projects of the thermal power plant in the Tennessee Valley from 1940 to 1965. The reasons are as follows
units.reusable_pattern: Announce the choice, then the reasons.
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide the selection criteria

units.rhetorical_move: argues the project both helps and harms
units.function: makes the environmental term necessary

original_instantiations: The plants supply energy and jobs, but they also burn fuel and discharge waste.
The harm is what forces the environmental cost into the appraisal.

units.source_excerpt: the construction of large thermal power plants can produce powerful electric power for the benefit of society, but also need to use a lot of primary energy and water resources
units.reusable_pattern: Grant the benefit, then the cost that comes with it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop either side

units.rhetorical_move: compresses the computation into one phrase
units.function: moves straight to the table of scores

original_instantiations: The computation is summarized and the scores are presented.
The reader is not shown the arithmetic, only the ranks.

units.source_excerpt: After a series of calculation in our long run model of the data from above, the variation values of different indexes are obtained.
units.reusable_pattern: Summarize the computation and point to the result.
prohibited_generalizations: do not pretend the arithmetic was shown

units.rhetorical_move: reads the inequality as a verdict
units.function: keeps the environmental cost inside the verdict

original_instantiations: The higher score means the project still has value once the environmental cost is inside.
The verdict names the cost it survives.

units.source_excerpt: Because G2>G1, that means construction project of Tennessee thermal power stations still have social value according to cost benefit analysis in a long-term perspective even incorporating environmental cost into the total cost.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the inequality, then what it means.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the even

units.rhetorical_move: recalls the assumption and calls it inaccurate
units.function: opens the test by disputing the earlier choice

original_instantiations: The equal weighting was assumed, and it is now called inaccurate.
The test begins by withdrawing the earlier assumption.

units.source_excerpt: In fact, it is not accurate because different decision makers have different priorities with respect to their preference.
units.reusable_pattern: Withdraw the assumption and give the reason.
prohibited_generalizations: do not keep the assumption while testing it

units.rhetorical_move: contrasts two kinds of decision maker
units.function: gives the range of the weight a meaning

original_instantiations: A caring government weighs the environment heavily, while a builder treats it as a small item.
The two extremes explain why the weight is freed.

units.source_excerpt: Benevolent governments may care more about environmental protection, while entrepreneurs may consider the environment as a small factor affecting cost.
units.reusable_pattern: Set the two decision makers against each other with while.
prohibited_generalizations: do not collapse the two into one preference

units.rhetorical_move: reads the figure as stability
units.function: says the adjusted model moves less

original_instantiations: Both lines settle toward the same value, but the adjusted one moves less.
The comparison is about stability, not about the verdict.

units.source_excerpt: We can see that both of them converge to 5 with the growth of a, but the model is more stable after adjusting the weight of air quality.
units.reusable_pattern: State the shared behaviour, then the difference.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the lines are identical

units.rhetorical_move: states the verdict holds for every weight
units.function: removes the decision maker's preference from the outcome

original_instantiations: The decision stays the same no matter which cost is emphasised.
The restatement drops the mathematics and keeps the decision.

units.source_excerpt: the decision to build a thermal power station will always be made regardless of the emphasis on economic cost or on environmental cost
units.reusable_pattern: State the invariance, then restate it in plain words.
prohibited_generalizations: do not extend the invariance past this project

units.rhetorical_move: matches the two verdicts to reality
units.function: offers the match as partial support

original_instantiations: The local schemes are being closed while the regional scheme is remembered as worthwhile, which supports the model only partly.
The support is hedged as partial.

units.source_excerpt: China's small paper mills are being gradually clamped down, while the development of Tennessee thermal power in the United States has brought great positive value in the history, which shows that our model is effective to some extent.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the two facts, then the hedged conclusion.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the hedge

units.rhetorical_move: names the motive and the remedy
units.function: moves from the private incentive to the public correction

original_instantiations: Builders chase profit and will not bear the cost, so the government has to put the cost back into the real bill.
The remedy is named as regulation or a tax.

units.source_excerpt: since businessmen are self-interested and pursue profit maximization, they may have no incentive to bear environmental costs. Therefore, the government should take this externality into full consideration
units.reusable_pattern: State the private motive, then the public response.
prohibited_generalizations: do not assume the builders internalize the cost themselves

units.rhetorical_move: names the instrument
units.function: says how the cost gets into the real bill

original_instantiations: The cost is brought inside the real bill by a rule or a tax.
The instrument is named and then glossed.

units.source_excerpt: correct the negative environmental benefits brought by land development by means of regulation or Pigovian tax. That is, government will internalize the environmental costs into the real costs of land construction.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the instrument, then gloss it with that is.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the instrument unnamed

units.rhetorical_move: claims coverage of both horizons
units.function: lists what the coverage includes

original_instantiations: The cost covers the present period and also the far period.
The strength is stated as a span, not a single feature.

units.source_excerpt: It not only includes the current economy-health cost, but also considers the environmental cost in the sense of sustainable development and ecology in the long run.
units.reusable_pattern: Span the strength with not only and but also.
prohibited_generalizations: do not reduce the strength to one horizon

units.rhetorical_move: explains why money was dropped
units.function: calls the forced pricing strained

original_instantiations: Pricing the far-horizon damage would be strained, so the comparison was turned into a scoring process.
The switch is defended by the weakness of the alternative.

units.source_excerpt: forced monetization is somewhat far-fetched due to the lack of monetization approaches for environmental costs caused by environmental degradation. Therefore, we converted the cost-benefit analysis into the analytic hierarchy process
units.reusable_pattern: Call the alternative strained, then give the replacement.
prohibited_generalizations: do not defend the switch without the reason

units.rhetorical_move: grounds the matrix in the residents' wishes
units.function: claims the measurement is close to the citizens

original_instantiations: The weights can follow a public survey, so the measurement stays near what the citizens want.
The closeness is offered as a strength.

units.source_excerpt: From the perspective of humanistic care, this cost measurement is close to the will of citizens.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the standpoint, then the closeness it claims.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the survey was actually carried out

units.rhetorical_move: calls the matrix rough and offers the better source
units.function: owns the weakness and names the repair

original_instantiations: The matrix rests on keyword counts, and a poll would be better if it can be done.
The weakness and the preferred source are given together.

units.source_excerpt: The selection of comparison matrix is relatively rough. In the case of insufficient information, our method is to select the quantity of academic keywords as the basis of people's attention. If feasible, the initial matrix should be selected according to the poll results.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the weakness, the cause, then the better source.
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide the keyword method

units.rhetorical_move: says the scoring cannot show a large gap
units.function: qualifies the benchmark

original_instantiations: The benchmark fails to show the gap when the return greatly exceeds the cost.
The failure is located in one situation.

units.source_excerpt: This scoring method needs to be evaluated, especially when the economic benefits of enterprises are much greater than the economic costs, which cannot reflect the gap perfectly.
units.reusable_pattern: State the need, then the situation where it fails.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the scoring is uniform

units.rhetorical_move: admits the benefit side was neglected
units.function: names the missing environmental benefit

original_instantiations: The analysis stays on the cost and leaves the environmental benefit out.
The omission is owned and postponed to later work.

units.source_excerpt: We focus our analysis on cost and pay less attention to benefit. We did not consider the environmental benefits of the project, which are important features of some green public projects.
units.reusable_pattern: State the imbalance, then the specific omission.
prohibited_generalizations: do not imply the benefit side was analysed

units.rhetorical_move: calls the time split vague
units.function: admits there is no boundary

original_instantiations: The split between the two horizons has no clear boundary.
The weakness is the absence of a line.

units.source_excerpt: The long-term and short-term time division is relatively vague, without clear boundaries.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the division and the boundary it lacks.
prohibited_generalizations: do not invent a boundary the paper does not give

units.rhetorical_move: reports that some projects turn negative
units.function: draws the advice from the result

original_instantiations: Once the environmental cost is counted, some projects turn negative, so the greener plan is advised.
The result and the advice share one sentence.

units.source_excerpt: The results show that in some cases, the actual value of some land use projects is negative when environmental costs are considered. So we suggest the planners should choose green construction plans as far as possible.
units.reusable_pattern: Report the result, then the suggestion.
prohibited_generalizations: do not say every project turns negative

units.rhetorical_move: lists the sources as numbered lines
units.function: keeps articles, books and web pages in one list

original_instantiations: Each source gets a number and its own line.
The list mixes journal articles, books and pages.

units.source_excerpt: [1] Chee, Y., 2004. An ecological perspective on the valuation of ecosystem services.
units.reusable_pattern: Give each source a number and one line.
prohibited_generalizations: do not retype the whole list
